opportunities.title: Trezor's Email Got Popped, Not Your Seed — But Here's Why That Distinction Won't Save the Next Victim
opportunities.why_now: Trezor confirmed a third-party breach sent phishing emails from its own legitimate domain, blurring the line users rely on to trust official comms.
opportunities.angle: Security teardown: explain the supply-chain vector, what Trezor did right (hardware isolation) vs. what phishing-from-legit-domain defeats, and a checklist for verifying comms going forward.

opportunities.title: A Family Was Murdered for a Cold Wallet — The Wrench Attack Isn't Theoretical Anymore
opportunities.why_now: A Mexican musician and his family were killed over a suspected multimillion-dollar cold wallet, a stark real-world escalation of the $5 wrench attack meme.
opportunities.angle: Sober, unflinching op-ed on physical security failures of self-custody culture — multisig, duress wallets, and why flaunting holdings is a death sentence, not flex.

opportunities.title: Liquid's $320M Exploit, Autopsied: How White Hats Clawed Back $270M and Why $9.2M Still Got Out
opportunities.why_now: Chainalysis published the full technical breakdown of the Liquid Network hack right as the network prepares to restart, with Cronos separately confirming leakage despite its Tectonic rollback.
opportunities.angle: Comparative postmortem: contrast Liquid's white-hat recovery against Cronos's incomplete rollback to show why 'we reversed it' headlines oversell actual security outcomes.

opportunities.title: OFAC Just Sanctioned a Multibillion-Dollar Scam Mall — Here's Why Xinbi Won't Be the Last
opportunities.why_now: Treasury/DOJ sanctioned Xinbi Guarantee and Secret Service froze $52.8M tied to it, the latest in a pattern of Telegram-based crypto scam marketplaces getting dismantled.
opportunities.angle: Explainer connecting the enforcement dots across OFAC, DOJ, and Secret Service actions — what Xinbi's business model reveals about the scam-market economy still operating in plain sight.

opportunities.title: LAPTOP's 99% Crash Wasn't Bots — It Was the Business Model
opportunities.why_now: Hunter Biden's LAPTOP memecoin blamed 'sniper bots' for a 99% launch-day collapse that left traders with six-figure losses, a script this channel's readers have seen a hundred times.
opportunities.angle: Pattern-recognition piece: walk through the thin-liquidity/sniper mechanics that make near-certain 99% dumps predictable, and why blaming bots is the tell that management knew exactly what would happen.
